blocks.text: The portrait of Jehovah as merciful, gracious, patient, forgiving, and compassionate belongs to a wider setting of covenant life, worship, kingship, and wisdom teaching. These backgrounds frame mercy and grace as realities expressed within the life of God’s people, while the psalm’s own description in verses 8–13 remains the controlling witness.

The mercy and grace celebrated here are read as themes that continue across Scripture, developing from Israel’s story into the New Testament witness. Psalm 103:8–13 therefore stands within that broader scriptural testimony while speaking in its own images of restrained anger, removed transgressions, and a father’s compassion.
